title: Mass and spring frequency
hook: Change attached mass and predict oscillation frequency.
misconception: oscillation frequency doubles when attached mass doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply f = (1/2π)√(k/m) to compare oscillation frequency when attached mass changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With an ideal mass–spring oscillator with fixed spring stiffness, f = (1/2π)√(k/m). When attached mass doubles, oscillation frequency becomes 1/√2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model f = (1/2π)√(k/m); scaling exponent -0.5. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider an ideal mass–spring oscillator with fixed spring stiffness, with a nonzero initial result. If attached mass triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on oscillation frequency?
recall.why: Apply f = (1/2π)√(k/m) under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 1/√3.
